prepared_template.title: Acute abdominal signs with massive proteinuria but no overt oedema
prepared_template.facts:
A boy under 10 years old with no reported medical history presented with severe abdominal pain and repeated vomiting since the previous evening. Temperature 36.9°C, blood pressure 103/54 mm Hg, pulse 119 beats/min.

Examination showed abdominal distension, right lower quadrant tenderness and rebound tenderness, without oedema or purpura.

Abdominal radiography showed dilated, gas-filled small-bowel loops. Ultrasonography showed a keyboard sign in a dilated small-bowel loop (diameter 15 mm; wall thickness 3.7 mm), with to-and-fro movement on supplemental video.

The ultrasonographic inferior vena cava-to-aorta ratio (IVC/Ao) was 0.4, below the 0.8 cut-off indicating intravascular volume depletion.

Laboratory findings: white blood cells 13.5×10⁹/L; haemoglobin 140 g/L; haematocrit 0.42 L/L; albumin 2.0 g/dL; BUN 11.5 mg/dL; creatinine 0.3 mg/dL (BUN/Cr ratio 38.3); Na 139 mEq/L; K 4.5 mEq/L; Cl 106 mEq/L; total cholesterol 204 mg/dL; triglycerides 30 mg/dL; C3 148 mg/dL; C4 30 mg/dL; D-dimer 1.3 µg/mL (normal <1.0 µg/mL); fibrinogen 544 mg/dL.

Urinalysis revealed high specific gravity. Massive proteinuria was confirmed by a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) of 27.1 g/g creatinine, without haematuria.

Recorded context: the keyboard sign and to-and-fro movement are described as characteristic ultrasonographic findings of small bowel obstruction, and the keyboard sign is described as suggestive of small bowel obstruction.

Availability limits: this is a constructed selected-record review at the initial assessment point. No documented initial working diagnosis is recorded in the supplied material at this point. Data on response to fluids, later imaging, steroid treatment, biopsy decisions and outcome are withheld and must not be assumed. Unreported findings are unknown, not normal.

prepared_template.reference: At this point, documented findings include peritonism (rebound tenderness) alongside signs reported as characteristic of small bowel obstruction, plus documented intravascular depletion. Safe next steps include early surgical involvement or clear escalation criteria, careful sodium-containing fluid resuscitation with monitoring, and repeat imaging within 12–24 hours as documented in the source (p-14). No treatment response, biopsy decision or outcome may be assumed.
